correctness.rationale: A positive increment needs opposite signs, and their two largest magnitudes are attained at distinct compartments when both are positive. Thus the adaptive increment is min(M_+,M_−). The Skellam series follows by summing the Poisson difference probabilities, and independent compartments and disjoint positive/negative categories give the exact tail by inclusion–exclusion for every k≥1. The probability of A=k,B=0 and the upper tail of A give log p_k=−k log k+O_λ(k), so thresholds (1±ε)log C/log log C have Cp_k tending to infinity or zero respectively. For the expectation, the lower threshold gives the lower bound, and the Poisson mass ratio bounds the sum of upper tails past the upper threshold by a geometric series with first term tending to zero after multiplying by C. The centered Skellam mgf rescaled by sqrt(2λ) converges to the normal mgf, and the optimizer is continuous, which gives the stated fixed-C limit in law including its atom at zero. With standard normal norming, C(1−Φ(u_C+x/a_C))→exp(−x), and substituting this into the same inclusion–exclusion formula gives the displayed minimum-of-two-Gumbels CDF. The proof needs no uploaded computations; the reported finite checks were not independently replayed. Neither a joint limit nor growth at fixed total inventory is asserted.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The relevant broader coverage is the pair identity plus general extremes, not the fixed-total complete-fusion expectation. For a positive maximum, use A_i restricted to B_i=0 as a lower envelope and the unrestricted A_i maximum as an upper envelope; conditionally the lower envelope has an independent Poisson sample of binomial size asymptotic to exp(−λ)C. The negative maximum has the same squeeze with A and B interchanged, so the minimum has the same probability scale by a union bound. A standard Poisson tail-ratio bound gives the matching mean. In the sequential regime, the prior Gaussian limit and classical normal tail entail the Gumbel-min law via the same independent occupancy calculation.
